notes.r-p6-01:0: Insertion, key C (only one elevator shut at a time). Near-correct A 'Both elevators will therefore be out of service until March 20' follows 'The work is expected to take five days' perfectly and 'therefore' makes it look like the natural conclusion. Deciding clue is in P2: 'The elevator that remains in service' and 'leave it free'. B (dates not yet set) is killed by P1 sentence 1 and the subject line; D (loading dock closed) by P2 sentence 3 and P3. Self band hard (L D B). Blind review: hard.
notes.r-p6-01:1: Pronoun, key A it. Near-correct B them: pulled by the nearest plural 'the stairs' and by 'two passenger elevators' in P1; C one ('leave one free') is a real pattern but needs two or more running. Deciding clue: singular 'the elevator that remains in service' in the previous sentence plus P1's 'only one at a time'. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-01:2: REVISED (was the tense blank; now the connector, key B unless). The delivery sentence now comes BEFORE the freight-elevator sentence, so when the reader reaches the blank nothing rules out a strict rule: 'should be postponed even if they are brought in through the loading dock early in the morning' (near-correct A). Deciding clue is the next paragraph: the freight elevator 'will be open to tenants for these deliveries from 6 to 8 a.m.' ('these deliveries' = the large-item deliveries; 6-8 a.m. = 'early in the morning'). because / although fail on logic. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-01:3: REVISED (was the connector; now the tense blank, key D will be). Near-correct A has been ('has been open to tenants ... each weekday' reads fine alone). 'During the work,' was removed from P2; the time cues are the e-mail date (March 9), P1 'will begin' on March 16, 'these deliveries' (the postponed future deliveries) and 'normally used only by building staff' in the same sentence. Self band medium (L D; B no).
notes.r-p6-02:0: Linking adverb, key D As a result. Near-correct A Nevertheless, helped by the negative word 'rejected' in the previous sentence. Deciding clue: 'far fewer rejected claims than they had with the paper forms' is a good result, so the switch follows from it. Otherwise / For example fail on meaning. Self band hard (L D B); the clue is the adjacent sentence, so the blind review may call it medium.
notes.r-p6-02:1: Adverb, key B still. Near-correct A no longer: after 'receipts are simply photographed ... and attached', 'no longer need to keep the originals' is the natural guess. Deciding clue is the next sentence, now made explicit per the blind review: 'Our auditors may ask to see the originals during the annual review.' Self band hard (L D B). Blind review: hard.
notes.r-p6-02:2: Insertion, key A ('This earlier date lets us repay claims in the month they are submitted'). Near-correct C 'Claims that arrive after that date will no longer be accepted' (a common rule, fits right after 'need to be submitted by the 5th') is contradicted by the next sentence (claims submitted late are repaid the following month). B 'This later date' needs the 15th-vs-5th comparison; D (paper accepted until year end) contradicts P1 'replace the paper forms ... starting October 1'. 'must be submitted' softened to 'need to be submitted' per the review. Self band hard (L D S). Blind review: hard.
notes.r-p6-02:3: REVISED (was the participle 'submitted', judged easy; now a word-form blank, key C late). Sentence: 'Claims submitted {4} will be repaid the following month instead.' Near-correct A lately: learners treat it as the adverb of 'late', and 'Claims submitted lately will be repaid ...' is grammatical; but 'lately' means 'recently', which does not fit the 5th-of-the-month deadline and the 'in the month they are submitted' contrast in the previous two sentences. lateness (noun) and latter (adjective only) cannot modify 'submitted'. 'latest' and 'later' were avoided as options because both can be read as adverbs meaning 'after the deadline'. Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-03:0: Insertion, key B ('Expanding the original bakery was never an option'), explained by the next sentence (narrow lot). 'however' removed from B and D per the review so it appears only once in the article. Near-correct A 'The company plans to close the Mill Road bakery once the new site opens': the narrow-lot sentence reads like the reason for closing. Deciding clue in P3 (Mill Road will concentrate on bread and keep baking some pastries) and P4 (no one has to move). C (two sites for years) contradicts P1 'Until now, everything ... at its original bakery'; D (ovens off at night) contradicts 'around the clock'. Self band hard (L D B). Blind review: hard.
notes.r-p6-03:1: Tense, key D began. Near-correct A will begin: 'will begin in March, and ... is due to open in October' is consistent inside the sentence. Only the dateline (June 12) and 'this autumn' in P1 rule it out. B has begun is the Taiwanese-learner trap (present perfect with 'in March'). Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-03:2: Conjunction, key C Until. REVISED context: the previous sentence is now 'The building has room for all of Corvell's pastry production, so Mill Road will be left to concentrate on bread', which closes the 'new site too small' reading the blind reviewer found for 'Once'. Near-correct A Once ('Once the new site is running at full capacity' is the stock phrase) now contradicts that sentence outright. Even though contradicts the October opening; In case is nonsense. Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-03:3: Vocabulary, key A opportunity. Near-correct B obligation (and C instruction): 'be given the obligation to transfer' reads fine alone. Deciding clue: previous sentence 'no current employee will be required to move'. Plain meaning contrast, so B no. Self band medium (L D).
notes.r-p6-04:0: Preposition, key A Unlike. Near-correct B Like: 'Like the printed magazine, the digital edition will reach you on the first of every month' is grammatical and sounds reassuring. Deciding clue in P1: the printed copy 'often arrives a week or more after the first of the month'. Despite / Except for fail on meaning. Self band hard (L D S).
notes.r-p6-04:1: Insertion, key C ('The new rate will apply to all subscriptions, including renewals'). Near-correct A 'Readers who have already renewed, however, will keep paying the old rate' is a common rule and fits right after the price cut; the next sentence (refund of the difference) kills it. D '$96 print price' is killed only by P3 ($72 + extra $30 = $102). B 'first price increase' contradicts the fall from $96 to $72. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-04:2: Relative pronoun, key D who. Near-correct A whom: 'our records' right after the blank looks like the subject, so the blank looks like an object; remove 'our records show' and the blank is the subject of 'have paid' (hypercorrection trap). Clue is in-sentence. Self band medium (L B S).
notes.r-p6-04:3: Conditional inversion, key B Should. Near-correct A Would: 'Would you prefer to keep receiving the magazine by mail' reads as a polite question until the comma and the imperative 'please check'. Had needs a past participle and a past counterfactual; Were needs 'Were you to'. Clue is in-sentence. Self band medium (L B).
